pr.title: coverage: Avoid splitting spans during span extraction/refinement
pr.description:
This PR removes or simplifies some of the steps involved in extracting coverage-relevant spans from MIR, and preparing them for use in coverage instrumentation metadata.

A common theme is that we now try harder to avoid modifying or combining spans in non-trivial ways, because those modifications present the most risk for weird behaviour or ICEs.

The main changes are:
- When extracting spans from MIR call terminators, try to restrict them to just the function name.
- Instead of splitting spans around “holes”, just discard any span that overlaps with a hole.
- Instead of splitting macro-invocation spans into two parts, truncate them to just the macro name and subsequent `!`.

---

This results in a lot of tiny changes to the spans that end up in coverage metadata, and a few changes to coverage reports. Judging by test snapshots, these changes appear to be quite minor in practice.
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.originalLogic: The pre-PR InstrumentCoverage span-extraction pipeline refined coverage spans by aggressively modifying spans. For Call/TailCall terminators it started from `terminator.source_info.span` and, when the callee constant started later, did `span = span.with_lo(constant.span.lo())`. For visible bang-macro invocations it split a span at `visible_macro.as_str().len() as u32 + 1` into a `before` part covering the macro name plus `!` and an `after` part covering the rest, pushing both as new spans. When dividing spans into hole-separated buckets, it split every covspan around each hole via `split_around_hole_span`, put the `before` pieces in the current bucket, and carried the `after` pieces into a `fragments` vector for the next hole; each resulting bucket was then explicitly re-sorted with `covspans.sort_by(compare_covspans)`. The PR states that these modifications/combinations are risky, so the new logic instead only uses a constant callee span when it is fully contained (`span.contains(constant.span)`), truncates visible macro spans with `source_map.span_through_char(covspan.span, '!')`, and discards spans that overlap a hole rather than splitting them. The PR also replaces the manual `from_fn`/`front`/`pop_front` drain helper with `pop_front_if`, which is a mechanical optimization and not the semantic change.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect/risky transformation is: (1) extend a call terminator span's low bound to the callee constant span's low bound whenever the constant starts later, without requiring containment; (2) split a visible bang-macro invocation span into exactly two spans at the byte offset `macro_name_len + 1`; (3) split each coverage span around every hole into `before` and `after` fragments, retaining both and carrying `after` fragments forward to later holes. These are the transformations to hold fixed or swap when constructing differential tests; they are not merely descriptions of the new implementation.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR of functions being instrumented by InstrumentCoverage, especially code with macro invocations (for example `assert_eq!`/`assert_ne!`), call or tail-call terminators whose `func` operand is a constant, and HIR-derived holes such as closures, async blocks, const blocks, and other non-user-code regions whose spans may overlap MIR statement/terminator spans. Spans may be macro-expanded, include non-ASCII identifiers, or span multiple lines.
analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage PR replacing risky span splitting/extension with containment-checked call spans, macro-name truncation, and hole-overlap discarding. It is a span-extraction/refinement robustness refactor, not a reproduced bug report; the only clearly non-semantic optimization is the `pop_front_if` drain helper.
analysis.trigger: Compiling with coverage instrumentation when MIR contains a Call/TailCall with a constant callee span, a visible bang-macro invocation span, or any extracted coverage span that overlaps a hole; the old code would then modify/split those spans, while the new code substitutes only contained constant spans, truncates macro spans through `!`, and drops hole-overlapping spans.
preconditions: InstrumentCoverage is extracting and refining coverage spans from MIR.
The input spans and holes are sorted; new code explicitly relies on this invariant after removing per-bucket sorting.
For the call-span change, the callee is an `Operand::Constant` and its span may or may not be contained in `terminator.source_info.span`.
For the macro change, the span's expansion kind is `ExpnKind::Macro(MacroKind::Bang, _)` and the source map can locate the `!` character.
For the hole change, `holes` are non-empty and some covspans may overlap them.
pitfalls: Using `with_lo` without a containment check can create a call span that starts at the callee but ends before the callee span or otherwise includes/excludes unrelated text; only replacing the whole span with `constant.span` when `span.contains(constant.span)` is safe under the new invariant.

Splitting a macro span by `macro_name.len() + 1` assumes the split point is valid and that the resulting two pieces correctly correspond to the macro name/`!` and the remainder; the new code instead uses `span_through_char(..., '!')`, which also matters for non-ASCII identifiers.

Splitting covspans around holes and carrying `after` fragments forward can retain spans that overlap the hole or produce buckets that are no longer internally sorted; the new code discards any span where `c.span.overlaps(hole.span)` and therefore no longer needs to sort each bucket.

Removing the per-bucket sort is only valid because the sorted input invariant plus `drain_front_while` and the final `Vec::from(input_covspans)` preserve sorted bucket contents; the patch asserts `input_covspans` and `holes` are sorted.

Coverage reports can legitimately change when sub-expression spans are discarded or truncated, as shown by the `assert_ne!` test being changed to `black_box(Foo(5))` and by coverage lines for macro argument/closing punctuation becoming uncovered; do not treat every snapshot change as a regression.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the existing coverage snapshot suites as the primary oracle: `tests/coverage/*.cov-map` (raw mapping bytes plus decoded `Code`/`Branch`/`MCDCDecision` mappings) and `tests/coverage/*.coverage` (line/region reports), plus `tests/mir-opt/coverage/*.InstrumentCoverage.diff` for the inserted `coverage Code { bcb }` statements. Build focused program pairs that differ only in the span operation: (a) a call whose constant callee span is fully contained versus one where the old `with_lo` extension would move the start outside/over the end; (b) a visible `assert_eq!`/`assert_ne!` macro span versus the same invocation with nested expressions, checking that only the macro name and `!` are retained; (c) a covspan that overlaps a hole (closure/async/const block) to compare old split-around-hole fragments against new discard-on-overlap; (d) non-ASCII identifiers before `!` to exercise `span_through_char`. Because no compiler was built here, describe expected `.cov-map`/`.coverage`/MIR-diff snapshots rather than claiming execution.
